subject: Life Skills
title: Pay Yourself First
description: A quick, practical guide to Pay Yourself First.

hook.text: The richest man in Babylon's secret, written in 1926: keep at least one-tenth of all you earn. Before anything else.

buildup.text: Most people save what is left after spending. Left-after-spending is usually zero. Reverse the order and savings happen.

discovery.text: Move savings out of your checking account on payday, before any bill or purchase. What remains is your spending budget.

twist.text: You will adjust spending downward without noticing. People adapt to the money they see available.

climax.text: Start with 5% if 10% feels impossible. Increase by 1% every three months. Within two years you hit 10% painlessly.

punchline.text: Save first. Spend what is left. Not the reverse.

quiz.question: Why does 'pay yourself first' work better than saving what is left?
options: Banks offer better rates for early savings
People adapt their spending to what remains after savings are removed
First-of-the-month money is worth more due to compound interest
